Note::remove_control_chars¶

Back to Note API Reference

Signature¶

Note Note::remove_control_chars() const

Delete Control Bytes, Keeping Tab And Newline¶

remove_control_chars() returns a new Note, same shape as the input, with the ASCII control bytes deleted from each cell — except tab (\t), newline (\n), and carriage return (\r), which are kept. The DEL byte (0x7F) is removed. Use it to sanitize text of stray control characters — bell, backspace, escape, NUL-adjacent bytes — that would corrupt a terminal or a log while preserving normal layout.

Non-ASCII bytes are not touched, so accented and non-Latin text passes through unchanged. Only the removed bytes disappear; nothing is trimmed or collapsed.

remove_control_chars is shape-preserving, cell-independent, and returns a fresh Note. Use keep_printable instead when tab and newline should also go, or keep_ascii when non-ASCII should go too.

Example 1: A Batch¶

const std::string s = std::string("alert") + '\x07' + "text\tkept\nkept café";
std::cout << pluss::note::print(
    pluss::make_note({s, "clean"}).remove_control_chars())
    << "\n";

Output¶

Note(shape=[2], dim=1, numel=2, encoding=utf8)
["alerttext\tkept\nkept café", "clean"]

The bell (\x07) is gone; the tab, the newline, and the é all remain.

See Also¶

  • Note::keep_printable: also removes tab, newline, and non-ASCII.

  • Note::keep_ascii: keeps ASCII controls, removes only non-ASCII.

  • Note::collapse_whitespace: normalise the spacing that remains.
